Name: belief_entrenchment_probing
Title: Frozen Minds: Probing and Unfreezing Internal Belief Entrenchment During LLM Reasoning
Short Hypothesis: As an LLM generates a multi-step reasoning trace, its internal belief about the answer to an item becomes progressively 'entrenched': the linearly-decodable belief representation stops updating in response to new evidence introduced later in the trace, even when that evidence should rationally shift it. This internal entrenchment is measurable per-step, precedes and predicts behavioral confirmation bias, and can be causally reduced by steering the residual stream to restore belief plasticity, improving truth-seeking on evidence-integration tasks. Step-wise decodability is a validated premise, not the contribution; the novel claims are (a) that internal plasticity decays and freezes at a locatable point in the trace before textual/logit commitment, and (b) that a targeted plasticity intervention selectively restores late-evidence sensitivity and reversal-item accuracy without making the model indiscriminately swayed by any late text.
Related Work: Prior work establishes that transformers linearly represent belief states (Transformers Represent Belief State Geometry, 2024; Constrained Belief Updates, 2025) and that a 'solvability belief' axis is decodable but causally inert for execution (Confidence is Not Competence, 2025). Behaviorally, the Martingale Score (2025) shows LLM reasoning violates Bayesian martingale updating (belief entrenchment) at the output level, and Confirmation Bias in CoT (2025) shows prior beliefs skew reasoning. The Hypocrisy Gap (2026) contrasts a static internal belief with the CoT text. NONE of these track the trajectory of the internal belief representation itself across reasoning steps, characterize *when/where* it freezes relative to evidence arrival, or test a causal intervention to restore plasticity. We reframe entrenchment as an internal, per-step representational dynamics phenomenon and ask whether it is a causally editable failure mode, distinguishing our proposal from behavioral (Martingale) and static-belief (Hypocrisy Gap) approaches. Closest work and delta: the Martingale Score (2025) measures non-Bayesian updating at the output level — we measure the internal belief trajectory and its temporal freezing; Confirmation Bias in CoT (2025) shows priors skew reasoning behaviorally — we localize when/where the internal belief stops updating; belief-state-geometry work (2024) characterizes static geometry — we characterize its dynamics under delayed disconfirming evidence and a causal rescue. Probing, patching, and steering are standard tools; the contributions are the read-time freezing phenomenon and the plasticity intervention. Released artifact: an ordered-evidence 'late-reversal' benchmark with comprehension-matched controls, a per-step plasticity metric, and an entrenchment head map.
Abstract: When a language model reasons step-by-step, its final answer often confirms a hypothesis formed early, even when later steps surface contradicting evidence, a behavior known as confirmation bias or belief entrenchment. Prior studies measure this behaviorally or contrast a single static internal belief against the reasoning text. We instead track the internal belief representation itself as it evolves across reasoning steps. We hypothesize that entrenchment is a representational dynamics phenomenon: an LLM's linearly-decodable belief about an item's answer initially updates with incoming evidence but then 'freezes,' becoming insensitive to later, decision-relevant evidence. We construct controlled evidence-integration tasks in which pieces of evidence pointing toward different answers are revealed in a specified order within the prompt or generated trace, so that the rationally-updated belief has a known ground-truth trajectory. We train linear belief probes on frozen open-weight models (Llama-3-8B, Qwen2.5-7B, Gemma-2-9B, and a reasoning-tuned R1-distilled model) and measure, at each step, (i) the probe belief, (ii) its agreement with the rational Bayesian trajectory, and (iii) a per-step plasticity score (belief change per unit of new evidence). We test whether plasticity decays over the trace, whether an early-freezing signature predicts final-answer errors, and whether it correlates with behavioral entrenchment metrics like the Martingale Score. Finally, we identify the layers/heads mediating freezing via activation patching and test a causal 'unfreezing' intervention: injecting a plasticity direction (contrastive activation addition derived from high- vs. low-plasticity steps) to restore late-evidence sensitivity. We evaluate with probe/rational-agreement curves, plasticity decay slopes, entrenchment-error AUROC, patching effect sizes, and post-intervention accuracy and fluency. So what: late-evidence neglect drives costly errors in medical-triage dialogue, multi-hop retrieval, and tool-augmented agents that must revise on new observations; an online plasticity intervention is a cheap engineering fix and the freezing phenomenon is a mechanistic account. We report both scientific (mechanistic explanation) and engineering (inference-time rescue) impact, and release the benchmark, metric, and head map. To keep the contribution crisp we treat decodability, freezing, and prediction (E1-E3) as primary and localization/intervention (E4-E5) as confirmatory.
Experiments:
Experiment 1 (H1 — an internal belief representation is linearly decodable and updates step-by-step): Tests that a per-step belief about the answer exists. Data: built from scratch, 4,000 ordered-evidence items (multi-clue deduction puzzles, sequential-evidence forecasting, updating-diagnosis vignettes, and synthetic entity-attribute clue tasks) each with a synthetic-set oracle Bayesian belief trajectory; split 70/15/15 by item. Model: Llama-3-8B, Qwen2.5-7B, Gemma-2-9B, DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-7B, all frozen; trainable component only a logistic-regression belief probe P(answer=A) on residual activations at each reasoning-step boundary, per layer; 5 seeds. Systems compared: belief probe vs. shuffled-label control. Decisive metric first: probe test AUROC for the current-favored answer at each step. Convincing: mean AUROC >= 0.80 with control at 0.50 +/- 0.05 on >=3 of 4 models. Indecision band: 0.60-0.70 means the belief is only weakly decodable and per-step trajectories are unreliable. Negative: < 0.60 means no decodable step-wise belief and the remaining experiments are not interpretable.

Experiment 2 (H2 — the belief freezes: plasticity decays across the trace): Tests that late, decision-relevant evidence stops moving the belief. Use the 'late-reversal' condition (early evidence favors A, decisive later evidence favors B) vs. a matched 'consistent' condition. Define per-step plasticity = |delta probe-belief| per unit of oracle-expected belief change. Decisive metric first: slope of plasticity vs. step position (reversal condition), and post-reversal rational-agreement = correlation between probe and oracle trajectory. Convincing: significantly negative plasticity slope (bootstrap 95% CI excludes 0) and post-reversal agreement < 0.3 while consistent-condition agreement > 0.6. Indecision band: post-reversal agreement 0.3-0.5 is partial entrenchment. Negative: no slope difference and high post-reversal agreement means beliefs stay plastic (no entrenchment).

Experiment 3 (H3 — early freezing precedes and predicts behavioral confirmation bias): Tests that the internal signature forecasts final-answer errors. Decisive metric first: AUROC using late-step plasticity to predict final-answer error on reversal items, compared against a log-prob confidence baseline and the behavioral Martingale Score computed on the same runs. Convincing: plasticity AUROC >= 0.70 and >= 0.05 above log-prob. Indecision band: 0.60-0.70 or within 0.05 of log-prob is weak added value. Negative: <= 0.60 or no gain over log-prob means the internal signature is not predictive.

Experiment 4 (H2 — localization of the freezing): Finds where stale belief is carried. Activation patching from post-reversal (updated) into pre-reversal (stale) runs; measure heads/layers whose patch restores late-evidence sensitivity in the probe. Decisive metric first: fraction of the entrenchment effect recovered by the top head set. Convincing: a reproducible <= 20-head set recovers >= 50%. Indecision band: diffuse recovery reported as distributed. Negative: no head exceeds 20% recovery.

Experiment 5 (H3 — causal unfreezing restores plasticity): Tests that steering re-opens late-evidence sensitivity. Build a plasticity CAA vector (high- minus low-plasticity step activations) applied during late steps, alpha swept to 2/4/8% residual norm. Systems compared: plasticity steering vs. random-direction steering. Decisive metric first: final-answer accuracy delta on reversal items; secondary: restored post-reversal probe-oracle agreement, and collateral GSM8K/MMLU-subset accuracy and perplexity. Convincing: >= 10-point accuracy gain on reversal items with < 3-point drop on consistent items and < 10% perplexity rise; random steering < 3-point gain. Indecision band: 3-10 point gain is suggestive. Negative: < 3 points beyond random, or the model becomes indiscriminately swayed by any late text (consistent-item accuracy falls > 5 points), means no clean causal plasticity handle.

Experiment 6 (H1,H3 — generalization): Apply frozen probe and steering vector across task domains and to naturalistic RAG prompts. Decisive metric first: transfer AUROC of the probe. Convincing: >= 0.70 and steering retains half its accuracy effect. Indecision band: 0.60-0.70 limited. Negative: <= 0.60 distribution-specific.

Experiment 7 (H1,H3 — temporal precedence and applied late-evidence setting): Tests that internal freezing precedes behavioral commitment and holds when decisive evidence arrives via retrieval/tool output. Data: a 1,000-item agentic subset (adapted multi-hop retrieval and tool-correction dialogues) where a decisive document/observation arrives late. Decisive metric first: lead time in steps between internal plasticity collapse and the point at which next-token logits commit to the early answer; secondary: reversal-item accuracy with vs. without the plasticity intervention in the agentic setting. Convincing: internal collapse precedes logit commitment by >= 1 step on a majority of reversal items and the intervention recovers >= 10 points of agentic reversal accuracy. Indecision band: simultaneous collapse/commitment is reported as co-occurring, not precedent. Negative: commitment precedes internal collapse means the internal signal is a readout, not a driver.
Risk Factors and Limitations: Belief 'freezing' may reflect that the model simply cannot parse late evidence rather than an entrenchment failure; the matched consistent/reversal design and evidence-comprehension checks help disentangle these. The internal belief may not be cleanly linearly decodable at every step, or may be distributed across layers, complicating per-step trajectories; we use multi-layer probes and report layerwise results. The plasticity steering direction could degrade fluency or overshoot (making the model unstable/gullible to any late text); we monitor perplexity, use small magnitudes, and evaluate on consistent-condition and general benchmarks. Oracle Bayesian trajectories are only exact on synthetic sets; naturalistic items rely on approximate rational baselines. Reasoning-tuned models may show qualitatively different dynamics than base models, which is itself an interesting comparison but limits universal claims. Results may not transfer to very large closed models. We prioritize E1-E3 plus one of E4/E5 for a single paper rather than claiming phenomenon+localization+intervention at once. Significance uses bootstrap CIs with multiple-comparison correction across layers/heads and preregistered falsification conditions (e.g., high post-reversal agreement falsifies freezing). Probe validity is checked against decoding from step text alone, the previous-step hidden state, and randomized evidence order.
